newsitem.title: USA: Clinton stretches lead over Dole -- Newsweek poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton stretches lead over Dole -- Newsweek poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton continues to pull away from Bob Dole in the race for the White House, with the latest Newsweek poll on Saturday showing him 26 percent ahead of his Republican challenger.
The Newsweek poll of 755 registered voters showed that if elections were held today 54 percent would vote for Clinton, 28 percent for Dole and seven percent for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot.
The poll, conducted Oct. 17-18, has a margin of error of four percent.
A similar Newsweek poll Oct. 2-3 showed Clinton ahead with 53 percent of the vote, Dole with 32 percent and Perot with seven percent.
About 71 percent of those polled felt campaign contributions bought too much influence in Washington for wealthy foreign families and business interests.

Thirty-four percent classified as "very important" recent allegations that Clinton had received improper campaign contributions from a powerful Indonesian banking and real estate company while 26 percent said they were only "somewhat important."
The daily Reuters tracking poll on Saturday showed Clinton ahead of Dole 44.6 to 36.8 percent with 5.1 percent support for Perot.
